stories.headline: NBA trade deadline: Big questions for Knicks, Thunder and other top teams
stories.summary: With the NBA trade deadline looming, which title contenders should -- and could -- make a deal to improve?
stories.body:
With the start of the 2026-27 NBA regular season in the rearview, the Feb. 11 trade deadline is just over the horizon, and it's never too early to start discussing which teams need to keep their options open and potentially add talent over the next three months.

Injuries have plagued the league early on, with the Oklahoma City Thunder and Minnesota Timberwolves both losing major cornerstones of their roster for an extended period of time. Do these Western Conference contenders need to start filling out their rotations, or can they survive without their superstars until the postseason? And after a shaky start to the season, do the defending champions New York Knicks need to rethink their run back to the Finals with some roster moves?

As teams settle into the season, our NBA insiders break down what 10 playoff contenders lack, the constraints shaping their trade options and what's in store as the deadline approaches.

Order is based on the top 10 teams in ESPN's Basketball Power Index (BPI) as of Tuesday, Nov. 10.

Jump to a contender:

BOS | CLE | DET

HOU | LAL | MIN

NYK | OKC | PHI | SA

1. San Antonio Spurs (10-2)
Projected record: 62-20

Chances to make the conference finals: 58.5%

What they're missing: The Spurs are on a winning streak even without any games from Tobias Harris, their big offseason acquisition. It's hard to find a hole in one of the league's most complete, well-rounded rosters. Their depth, however, could use some improvement, so they won't be stuck playing deep from their bench with the likes of Jordan McLaughlin if one of their three guards goes down with an injury, as they did in the playoffs last year. -- Zach Kram

What they can pull off: The Spurs have the draft assets to swing a deal, but that does not mean general manager Brian Wright will look to be aggressive. With one of the best records last year, San Antonio elected to stand pat.

If the Spurs do look to make a move, they have an unprotected 2027 first-round pick from Atlanta and three additional tradeable first-rounders. They also have swap rights in 2028 (via Boston, if Nos. 2-30), 2030 (the most favorable of San Antonio, Dallas, Minnesota (if Nos. 2-30) and 2031 (via Sacramento). San Antonio has 12 tradeable second-rounders.

Keep an eye on whether San Antonio is willing to take back salary that stretches past 2026-27. With Victor Wembanyama's extension starting next season and sixth man Keldon Johnson a free agent, San Antonio is only $11 million below the luxury tax in 2027-28. -- Bobby Marks

What's next for San Antonio? San Antonio plans to play out the season with what's on the roster despite owning plenty of assets to make a move at the trade deadline. The Spurs appear to be somewhat thin at the center spot behind Luke Kornet, but the staff has been pleased with the progress made by rookie Tarris Reed Jr. in such a short time.

San Antonio understands that over the next two years, the roster could become expensive, with the club expected to sign Stephon Castle to an extension this summer, followed by an extension for Dylan Harper in the summer of 2028. Besides that, the Spurs are already experiencing somewhat of a numbers problem due to all the depth they've accumulated.

"There's not enough minutes to go around," coach Mitch Johnson said. "Unfortunately, I've got to play the bad guy and I'm not always going to be right. But I've got to make tough decisions in regards to only 240 minutes." -- Michael C. Wright

2. Oklahoma City Thunder (8-4)
Projected record: 58-24

Chances to make the conference finals: 43.5%

What they're missing: The Thunder are missing lots of rotation players, and their activity at this trade deadline will depend a great deal on when -- or whether -- they can project those injured players to return. Nique Clifford is another body on the perimeter, but he doesn't seem like a playoff difference-maker, so general manager Sam Presti might still be on the search for another defensively minded wing who can backfill some of the production of the injured Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace. -- Kram

What they can pull off: The Nov. 8 trade for Clifford does not eliminate Oklahoma City from making another trade. While the Thunder do not have a roster spot, they do have the $5.4 million expiring contract of Nikola Topic and the $4.9 million salary of a former first-round pick.

Because they are over the first apron, Oklahoma City cannot take back additional salary if either player is traded. The Thunder also have three trade exceptions ($5.8, $11.3, $17.7 million), seven tradeable first-round picks (including three in June) and 19 second-rounders. -- Marks

What's next for Oklahoma? Presti will be patient. The Thunder addressed the need for defensive-minded wing depth by making a buy-low trade for 2025 first-round pick Clifford, parting with a pair of second-round picks to acquire a player who has two seasons remaining on his rookie deal. Oklahoma City will explore the market for opportunities to upgrade over the next few months, but a big splash would be a big surprise.

It's not Presti's style, as the Thunder haven't made a major midseason trade since getting Kendrick Perkins in 2011. Yes, Presti has plenty of picks that could be used to put together a blockbuster deal. But he also has to prioritize future finances with the goal of keeping a contender-quality supporting cast around Shai Gilgeous-Alexander throughout his prime. -- Tim MacMahon

3. Boston Celtics (10-2)
Projected record: 59-23

Chances to make the conference finals: 57%

What they're missing: The Celtics rank only 22nd in defensive rebounding rate, which is an anomaly for a team coached by Joe Mazzulla. Boston has ranked 11th or better in this stat in every other year with Mazzulla at the helm, per Cleaning the Glass. This issue should be fixable based on Boston's roster, with the likes of Mitchell Robinson and Jayson Tatum -- an excellent rebounder for his position -- chipping in. If it continues, Boston might be in the market for another big body who can help grab rebounds in the playoffs. -- Kram

What they can pull off: Last season, the Celtics were one of the league's more active teams ahead of the trade deadline. The four separate trades dropped Boston below the luxury tax while also creating a $27.7 million trade exception. The exception is available until February, but the first apron hard cap prevents Boston from using more than $10 million of it.

This year, the Celtics do not have to trim payroll but do need to keep an eye on the luxury tax, which they are currently $1.75 million below. Boston's most valuable asset could be its open roste spot. Because they are below the first apron, the Celtics will be able to sign a waived player with a preexisting salary of $15 million or more -- Marks

What's next for Boston? Finding another big man could be high on the Celtics' list. One thing the Celtics have learned from the Knicks is not overtaxing Mitchell Robinson, who plays well in spurts, and keeping him around the 20-minute mark is ideal. Keeping Tatum and Paul George fresh would be paramount as well, especially with Tatum still working his way back to his new normal in his first full season following an Achilles injury in 2025. The $27 million trade exception could go a long way, especially if they view the Eastern Conference as winnable. -- Vincent Goodwill

4. Houston Rockets (9-3)
Projected record: 55-27

Chances to make the conference finals: 23.8%

What they're missing: Only two Rockets perimeter players are shooting better than 37% on 3-pointers this season, and one of them is Bogdan Bogdanovic, whose injury track record suggests it might not be safe to count on him over the full season. Kevin Durant and Reed Sheppard should improve as the season continues, but it might behoove Houston to grab one more shooter in the meantime. -- Kram

What they can pull off: The Rockets have two appealing trade assets in this upcoming draft: the right to swap with Brooklyn and an unprotected first-round pick (via the Phoenix Suns). Houston has four additional first-round picks available to trade, a $13.3 million trade exception and an open roster spot. The Rockets are allowed to use the full exception and still exceed the first apron. -- Marks

What's next for Houston? Despite owning plenty of assets and a trade exception, it's likely Houston will continue -- like last season -- to refrain from making any moves. Especially now that its roster has been revamped with the offseason additions of Bogdanovic and Marcus Smart, along with the return of point guard Fred VanVleet. The overall size throughout the roster gives the Rockets plenty of flexibility to utilize multiple lineups and combinations of players without sacrificing production and performance. VanVleet's absence last season somewhat sped up the development of Sheppard, Amen Thompson, Tari Eason and Jabari Smith Jr.

Still, Houston could probably use some depth at the center position, given the injury concerns regarding Steven Adams (right calf strain) and Clint Capela (right ankle sprain), who are both expected to return to the lineup soon. But unless the Rockets encounter a deal they can't refuse at the deadline, it's likely they stand pat. -- Wright

5. New York Knicks (6-5)
Projected record: 54-28

Chances to make the conference finals: 42%

What they're missing: The Knicks had, by definition, a championship-level roster last season, and the only player they lost was Robinson. Andre Drummond has served as a serviceable replacement so far, and it's difficult to imagine New York finding many better options on the trade market. But if one presents itself, then that's the clearest spot on New York's roster worth improving. -- Kram

What they can pull off: The Knicks faced the same limitations last season but were still able to trade for backup guard Jose Alvarado. This season, New York is $809,000 below the second apron and is not allowed to sign a player until Feb. 14. The Knicks can use Pacome Dadiet's $3 million expiring contract in a trade but cannot take back more salary. New York is not allowed to sign a player waived who had a preexisting salary of $15 million or more. The Knicks have one first-round pick and 12 second-rounders available to trade. -- Marks

What's next for New York? The Knicks are putting off contract issues until the offseason and there's not a lot of flexibility, especially with owner James Dolan proclaiming he won't go into the second apron. If Mikal Bridges continues to struggle, do the Knicks start to canvas the league? But then again, he's owed over $116.5 million over the next three seasons, including a player option in 2029-30. The hope is that he turns it around similar to last season, because this team is in need of shot creation and shotmaking. -- Goodwill

6. Los Angeles Lakers (11-2)
Projected record: 54-28

Chances to make the conference finals: 13.9%

What they're missing: The Lakers have the best offense in the league but rank in the bottom half on the other end of the floor, and specifically they're 28th in defensive rebounding rate, ahead of only the Bulls and Suns. Kevon Looney is not the answer at backup center behind Walker Kessler, and although Sandro Mamukelashvili is a decent option, it's safe to add the Lakers to the long list of teams that could use another competent bruiser on their bench. -- Kram

What they can pull off: The Lakers depleted their draft assets in the Kessler sign-and-trade which left them with the right to swap their 2028 first-rounder as their most significant remaining draft asset. The Lakers have three tradeable second-rounders (from 2031 to 2033, with two belonging to the Washington Wizards).

From a roster standpoint, Los Angeles could look to package the contracts of Jaden Hardy ($6 million) and Jarred Vanderbilt ($12.4 million) for a player earning $26 million or below. Despite being hard-capped at the first apron, the Lakers are $8.1 million under and are allowed to take back additional salary. Los Angeles has 15 guaranteed contracts and would need to waive or trade a player to open a roster spot. -- Marks

What's next for Los Angeles? After looking into trade packages to clear up a roster spot during the preseason, the Lakers ultimately had to waive former first-round pick Dalton Knecht in order to cut down to the maximum 15-player allotment. Coach JJ Redick has pretty much stuck to a 10-man rotation so far, with Vanderbilt overtaking Looney in the depth chart when Mamukelashvili isn't in as the stretch 5.

Redick still has to see what he has in second-year forward Adou Thiero and rookie Cameron Carr, although neither figures to be the solution to L.A. ranking second-to-last in the league in rebounding. Still, as one Eastern Conference executive told ESPN, "so long as Doncic, Reaves and Kessler stay healthy, the Lakers will be fine." -- Dave McMenamin

7. Minnesota Timberwolves (8-3)
Projected record: 54-28

Chances to make the conference finals: 26%

What they're missing: Entering the season, it seemed as if the Timberwolves' big issue was going to be frontcourt depth after they traded Julius Randle and Naz Reid in the offseason. But second-year Frenchman Joan Beringer has done an excellent job backing up his countryman, Rudy Gobert, and Trey Lyles, after a season out of the NBA, has performed surprisingly well at the backup power forward spot. Does Minnesota trust that that will continue, though, or would the team rather pursue a sure thing at the position? -- Kram

What they can pull off: The Timberwolves were one of the big winners last February when they acquired Ayo Dosunmu. Because of that trade and the offseason addition of LaMelo Ball, Minnesota's draft assets are limited. They have no first-round picks available to trade and one second-rounder (2030 via Memphis; if Nos. 51-60).

One player to watch could be Cody Williams, who is on an expiring $6 million contract after Minnesota declined his team option for next season. Apron rules prevent Minnesota from taking back more salary than they send out, so the return of Donte DiVincenzo, who tore his Achilles during the 2026 playoffs, could be the Timberwolves' big addition at the deadline. -- Marks

What's next for Minnesota? Keep biding time until Anthony Edwards' return. Minnesota should be thrilled with how it has played since its franchise guard underwent knee surgery after playing just four games to start the season. The Timberwolves are 5-2 without Edwards and boast the NBA's top-ranked defense. The schedule will get tougher, but they have held up well in the face of a potentially season-altering injury.

Ball continues to assimilate well to his new surroundings after an offseason trade, and fellow newcomer Jonathan Kuminga has made a good first impression after so-so stops with the Warriors and Hawks. Meanwhile, Dosunmu has been excellent as Edwards' stand-in replacement.

With Edwards projected to return as soon as late December or early January, Minnesota should have plenty of time to evaluate its full roster before the Feb. 11 trade deadline. -- Ben Golliver

8. Detroit Pistons (7-3)
Projected record: 55-27

Chances to make the conference finals: 44.4%

What they're missing: The Pistons' greatest need is the same as it has been for the last 18 months: a second scorer and playmaker next to Cade Cunningham. Duncan Robinson is the only other perimeter player averaging more than 12 points per game. And although Daniss Jenkins has done an admirable job as a backup, he's not a championship-level No. 2 option. Luckily, the Pistons have plenty of trade assets they could use in a deal for a fellow star. -- Kram

What they can pull off: The Pistons are among a handful of teams that control each of their next seven first-round picks. They can trade up to four and can swap in each season. Detroit also has 11 seconds available. And, despite $90 million committed to Cunningham and Jalen Duren this season, Detroit is $14.5 million under the first apron hard cap.

However, putting together a trade package without including a starter or key rotation piece could be difficult. To match salary, the Pistons have only the sizable contracts of John Collins ($17 million), Robinson ($16 million) and Isaiah Joe ($11.3 million). None have guaranteed salary obligations past this season.

For Detroit to use its $5.2 million or $15 million trade exception, it would need to open a roster spot. -- Marks

What's next for Detroit? The Pistons once again look poised to be among the top teams in the East during the regular season, even without making a move at the deadline. A year ago at the deadline, with a young team playing better than expected, Detroit chose not to rock the boat. This front office has chosen patience in letting its core of young players grow so far, so it's worth watching if an opportunity presents itself for a bigger swing and how the Pistons handle it this time around. -- Jamal Collier

9. Philadelphia 76ers (9-3)
Projected record: 49-33

Chances to make the conference finals: 21.1%

What they're missing: The 76ers don't have proper championship-level depth at center behind Joel Embiid, who is the single greatest injury risk for any team in the championship picture. Lineups with LeBron James at center can function on occasion, but that's not a permanent solution, and with Ariel Hukporti out for the season after tearing his Achilles, Philadelphia needs a better backup big man ahead of Jabari Walker and Adem Bona. -- Kram

What they can pull off: The 76ers have an open roster spot and Hukporti's $3.4 million expiring contract. Because they are $1.8 million under the first apron hard cap, they are allowed to take back up to $5.2 million of salary. They also have 10 second-round picks available to use in a trade. Philadelphia can sign a player with its open roster spot starting on Dec. 4. -- Marks

What's next for Philadelphia? Coach Nick Nurse said that big man Dominick Barlow, who has missed all of this season with a back injury, is expected to be cleared for on-court activities by mid-November. The Sixers are thin in the frontcourt, with Bona missing time with a neck injury, Hukporti out for the season and Tacko Fall missing time with a quad injury.

For now, the Sixers have been excited by how Walker has played as the team's backup center. Walker, too, missed time with a knee injury but has proven to be the team's most consistent backup center option this season. He had his best game this season in a win over the Bulls, finishing with nine points and 11 rebounds.

"He probably deserves to play more, to be honest," Nurse said this season. -- Kris Rhim

10. Cleveland Cavaliers (6-6)
Projected record: 47-35

Chances to make the conference finals: 11.8%

What they're missing: Cleveland ranks 29th in the league in defensive turnover rate, per Cleaning the Glass, ahead of only the woeful Milwaukee defense. This is still a decent defensive unit overall, thanks to the efforts of Evan Mobley and Jarrett Allen near the rim. But Cleveland's backcourt looks tremendously exploitable in the playoffs; even reserves Sam Merrill and rookie Meleek Thomas are more offensively minded. The Cavaliers are in desperate need of another perimeter stopper. -- Kram

What they can pull off: Five players (Mobley, Allen, Donovan Mitchell, Peyton Watson and James Harden) combine to earn 85% of the cap this season, making a trade difficult unless they are willing to part ways with Allen, or reserves Merrill and Jaylon Tyson. The Cavaliers are $45,000 below the first apron this season and have no tradeable first-round picks and only one second-rounder available. Cleveland can fill their open roster spot starting on April 9. -- Marks

What's next for Cleveland? After Harden took the place of Darius Garland at last season's deadline, the Cavs brought back their core four, believing that continuity will make a difference this season. But Cleveland is currently leaning on some younger players, such as Tyson, Thomas and Tyrese Proctor to fill out its depth off the bench. Keep an eye out for whether that trio can continue to produce or if the Cavs will look for moves similar to last season's deadline when they added veterans such as Dennis Schroder and Keon Ellis in an attempt to fortify their depth. -- Collier

stories.headline: 2026 NFL midseason report: Questions, stats for all 32 teams entering second half
stories.summary: The 2026 NFL season has hit the midway point. Here's what to watch in the second half, key QB stats and fantasy nuggets for all 32 teams.
stories.byline: NFL Nation reporters and Eric Moody
stories.body:
Nine weeks of the 2026 NFL season have passed. Some teams are riding high, while others are grasping for wins.

Much of what we believed we knew when it all began in September has been validated -- but lots of surprises, blockbuster trades and injuries have changed the course of our early-season predictions.

AFC South-leading Jacksonville went all-in on the defensive side with a trio of trades before the deadline this week, while John Harbaugh has the NFC East-leading New York Giants believing they hired the right man. No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza has yet to take the reins in Las Vegas but will this week after another big trade; there's not a single rookie who has stood out enough so far to say that the race for ROY isn't wide open. The NFC North remains the strongest division halfway through the season, while both Super Bowl participants have looked shaky of late. Of note, neither Seattle (11) nor New England (16) was ranked in the FPI top 10 at this point last season.

With that in mind, ESPN's 32 NFL team reporters took part in a midseason reset. Here, they lay out what they've learned through the first nine games and frame what's to come over the final nine weeks and beyond. Teams are ranked below by where each stands in ESPN's Football Power Index (FPI) rankings, and each club's current odds to win the division are also included as well as Eric Moody's non-QB fantasy football nuggets.

Jump to a team:

ARI | ATL | BAL | BUF | CAR | CHI | CIN

CLE | DAL | DEN | DET | GB | HOU | IND

JAX | KC | LAC | LAR | LV | MIA | MIN

NE | NO | NYG | NYJ | PHI | PIT | SF

SEA | TB | TEN | WSH

San Francisco 49ers
FPI rank: 1

Chances to make the playoffs: 99.3%

Chances to win their division: 94.6%

First-half storyline: The 49ers have jumped to a 7-1 start despite more injuries to key players, including to DE Nick Bosa (calf) and WR Mike Evans (Achilles tendinitis). But the Niners have again overcome those issues to find themselves in the driver's seat for the NFC's No. 1 seed with wins against three of the last four teams in the 2025 playoffs.

QB stat to know: Brock Purdy leads the NFL with a QBR of 82.5 and is firmly in the mix for the NFL's Most Valuable Player award. Perhaps more important given the other injury issues is that Purdy has started and finished all eight games, providing stability at the game's most important position.

Second-half storyline: Despite the hot start, the 49ers believe they can be better. Some of that will depend on health, but San Francisco has five starters in their first or second seasons -- and even more youngsters in key roles. If those players continue to develop, it could push the Niners to another level. -- Nick Wagoner

Fantasy nugget: Brock Purdy started the season averaging 27.0 fantasy PPG in the first three games. Since then, he has scored 18.1 fantasy PPG and has topped 20 points just once. He has the fourth-toughest remaining QB schedule, with games against the Vikings, Seahawks, Rams and Chiefs still on tap. It may be worth putting him on the trade block this week. -- Moody

Buffalo Bills
FPI rank: 2

Chances to make the playoffs: 99.8%

Chances to win their division: 96.3%

First-half storyline: Historic offense, problematic defense: The Josh Allen-Joe Brady partnership is a huge argument for continuity, with the Bills scoring at rates comparable to those of the best offenses in NFL history. But coordinator Jim Leonhard's defense, especially the secondary, is leaky and still figuring out communication issues far too late in the season.

QB stat to know: Allen has maintained a league-leading and career-best yards per attempt average (8.6) despite an injury that kept his best deep threat (WR DJ Moore) out of the lineup for the better part of four games. Even if it's not Brady's primary emphasis, the 2026 Bills are more explosive than they were even in Allen's best years.

Second-half storyline: The Thanksgiving to Christmas gauntlet: From Thanksgiving Day through Christmas Day, the Bills will play five consecutive games against contenders: Kansas City, at New England, at Green Bay, Chicago, at Denver. It's the toughest stretch of the season at the most important point of the season, and should decide whether the Bills hold on as AFC Super Bowl favorites. -- Nick Suss

Fantasy nugget: DJ Moore has a 26% target share, 41% air yard share and 14.3 fantasy PPG in his four full games. That is high-end WR2 production, but he will be tested to maintain it, as he has the toughest remaining fantasy schedule for WRs. -- Moody

Cincinnati Bengals
FPI rank: 3

Chances to make the playoffs: 98.6%

Chances to win their division: 79.5%

First-half storyline: Joe Burrow has officially found his groove, and the offense has never been better. The Bengals are third in points per drive (2.82), first in third-down conversion percentage (53.6%) and in fewest number of drives without a first down (18.3%). The engine that is built to lead the team is doing exactly that.

QB stat to know: Burrow has been otherworldly at stretching the field vertically, which is as much a credit to Burrow as it is to his star receivers -- Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. On throws of 15 air yards or more, Burrow has a 99.3 QBR and a whopping 18.1% completion percentage over expectation, per ESPN Research.

Second-half storyline: Can the offense continue its torrid pace? The offense has masked the defensive inconsistencies that have popped up in various moments. Third downs and allowing big rushing plays have been issues. But if the Bengals can keep forcing turnovers and keep their defensive red zone efficiency high (currently fifth), that might be enough. -- Ben Baby

Fantasy nugget: The Bengals have arguably the best passing attack in the NFL at the moment. Joe Burrow is the fantasy QB2, while Tee Higgins and Ja'Marr Chase are both top-five WRs. That will be tested as the Bengals have the seventh-toughest remaining fantasy schedule for QBs and third-toughest for WRs. Meanwhile, struggling Chase Brown has the third-best fantasy RB schedule. -- Moody

Jacksonville Jaguars
FPI rank: 4

Chances to make the playoffs: 98.8%

Chances to win their division: 93.4%

First-half storyline: The Jaguars are beating teams at a historic pace. They have four victories by 23 or more points, which is the most in a single season in franchise history. They're also the fifth team since 1999 with four victories by 23 or more points in the first eight games of the season -- three of the previous four teams that did that reached the Super Bowl, per ESPN Research.

QB stat to know: Trevor Lawrence has the NFL's lowest off-target percentage at 9.2%, which is by far the best percentage of his career (15% in 2025 was his previous best). Coach Liam Coen has praised Lawrence's footwork, which was the first thing he worked to fix in the spring before his first season as coach in Jacksonville in 2025, as a reason for his improved accuracy.

Second-half storyline: The Jaguars must keep the pass rush from being a liability. They are seventh in pressure rate but have only 16 sacks -- just four ahead of last-place Miami. Edge rushers Josh Hines-Allen and Travon Walker only have a combined five sacks. That's not going to be good enough against Caleb Williams, Aaron Rodgers, C.J. Stroud and Dak Prescott, who are all left on their schedule. -- Mike DiRocco

Fantasy nugget: Bhayshul Tuten is 15th among RBs in fantasy PPG and is third in the NFL in forced missed tackles rate. Tuten leads the Jags in goal-line carries and has scored three of their four goal-line TDs. In fact, he and Kenneth Walker III are the only RBs in the NFL with at least three rushing and receiving touchdowns this season. -- Moody

Denver Broncos
FPI rank: 5

Chances to make the playoffs: 96.6%

Chances to win their division: 57.0%

First-half storyline: Despite some fairly epic struggles on offense, the Broncos are the league's foremost escape artist. Of their seven wins, five are in one-score games and they have won an NFL-record 16 consecutive one-score regular-season games dating back to last season. As right tackle Mike McGlinchey said: "Maybe it's OK that we defy logic.''

QB stat to know: While he continues to put together his best work in the moments that matter the most, Bo Nix and the Broncos' offense as a whole have been unable to consistently put big plays together. Nix is 30th among 31 qualifying quarterbacks in air yards per attempt (5.9), ahead of only Patrick Mahomes. The difference is Mahomes and his teammates have created more catch-and-run yardage after those throws as Mahomes is ninth in the league in yards per attempt overall (7.7) while Nix is 28th (6.0).

Second-half storyline: The injuries in the secondary are a growing concern -- the Broncos have had four starters in the group miss at least two games this season -- but the offense's inability to make things easier on itself will really determine just how much of a postseason threat this team can be. They are tied for 29th in plays of at least 20 yards, ahead of only the Titans and Eagles, and are 30th in three-and-out drives (a whopping 28.3% of their possessions), ahead of only the Vikings and Eagles. -- Jeff Legwold

Fantasy nugget: Jonah Coleman has led Broncos RBs in snaps in each of the past three weeks, reaching 82% in Week 9. He leads the Broncos' backfield in explosive run rate, forced missed tackles rate and yards after contact per carry. Denver has the best remaining fantasy schedule for RBs, which gives Coleman league-winning potential. -- Moody

Chicago Bears
FPI rank: 6

Chances to make the playoffs: 90.4%

Chances to win their division: 41.6%

First-half storyline: The Bears firmly established themselves as a top NFC contender with a 7-2 record at their Week 10 bye. Their first-half trajectory sparked an all-in approach when they gave up three draft picks to land All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons, which paid instant dividends on defense. Caleb Williams returned from his hamstring injury a more efficient passer, and the Bears have not trailed at any point over their past four games (all wins) as they rank seventh in scoring (26.8 PPG).

QB stat to know: Williams leads the NFL in completion percentage (82.8%) when not pressured. He is ahead of the pace for the highest single-season completion percentage in that situation by a season-qualifying quarterback since ESPN first tracked pressures in 2009.

Second-half storyline: Most Bears games during the back half of the season will carry the intensity of playoff matchups. Chicago faces four NFC North opponents during Weeks 12-18 and needs to gain ground in the division after early losses to Minnesota and Green Bay. The Bears also play two division leaders in Jacksonville (first, AFC South) and Buffalo (first, AFC East), both of which rank top four in scoring. -- Courtney Cronin

Fantasy nugget: Luther Burden III has averaged 20.1 fantasy PPG in the four games since Caleb Williams returned, with at least 17 points in all four. For the season, the only WRs averaging more than 20.1 fantasy PPG are Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Puka Nacua and CeeDee Lamb. And Burden might stay hot, as the Bears have the fifth-best remaining fantasy WR schedule. -- Moody

Kansas City Chiefs
FPI rank: 7

Chances to make the playoffs: 95.9%

Chances to win their division: 42.6%

First-half storyline: The biggest improvement on the roster -- and a reason the Chiefs are back to being contenders in the AFC -- is the arrival and elite production of running back Kenneth Walker III. Walker and quarterback Patrick Mahomes have lifted the Chiefs to a 6-2 start. The defense has played its part, too, by creating 11 takeaways.

QB stat to know: Mahomes hasn't completed a pass of over 20 air yards since Week 4, when the Chiefs beat the Raiders and receiver Tyquan Thornton suffered a dislocated ankle that required surgery. Since then, Mahomes has had to matriculate the ball down the field with short passes and passes that are completed behind the line of scrimmage.

Second-half storyline: Mahomes left Sunday's game with a right elbow injury, one that could linger for the remainder of the season. The reason Mahomes suffered his injury is because the Chiefs' pass protection, with rookie left tackle Kahlil Benson and right tackle Jaylon Moore, has been lacking. Can Benson and Moore improve to give Mahomes enough time to operate the Chiefs' passing attack? -- Nate Taylor

Braelon Allen played more snaps (56%) but saw fewer opportunities (eight carries, two targets). This dings Hall's value a bit, but he remains an RB2. Allen, who is tied for the league lead in explosive run rate, is a flex option. -- Moody

Philadelphia Eagles
FPI rank: 29

Chances to make the playoffs: 0.1%

Chances to win their division: First-half storyline: Absences and poor coaching. The loss of quarterback Jalen Hurts (blood clots), right tackle Lane Johnson (retirement) and center Cam Jurgens (trade) coupled with a host of injuries has sapped this team from a talent standpoint. Even so, the Eagles shouldn't be dead last in the NFC standings. From the constant blown assignments along the offensive front to consistent underperformance in the second half, the coaches' fingerprints are all over this seven-game slide.

QB stat to know: Eagles signal-callers have been pressured on 40% of their dropbacks and have been blitzed 118 times -- the fourth-highest rate in both categories. The formula has been pretty simple: Bring heat against an offensive operation that is not in sync with its protection calls. The opposition has had success with this approach whether it's Hurts, Tanner McKee or Joe Milton under center. Philadelphia ranks 29th in passing yards per game (172).

Second-half storyline: Can Nick Sirianni save his job? He has built up equity after making the playoffs in each of his first five seasons, complete with a Super Bowl title. But things are a mess, particularly on offense -- the side of the ball where his expertise lies. Turnover is coming to the offensive staff. Will Sirianni help oversee the changes, or will he be a part of them? -- Tim McManus

Fantasy nugget: Touchdowns have kept Saquon Barkley afloat the past three weeks, but he has struggled to produce at his normal level as he plays through injury. He has averaged 2.3 and 1.7 yards per carry in his past two games and is seeing a reduced workload. For the time being, he is no longer a must-start, but volume keeps him as an RB2. -- Moody

Los Angeles Chargers
FPI rank: 30

Chances to make the playoffs: Chances to win their division: First-half storyline: The failure of head coach Jim Harbaugh to stem the bleeding. It's not just that offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel hasn't jelled with quarterback Justin Herbert. The steady hand on the wheel in Harbaugh has been anything but. Los Angeles shows no signs of improvement and has yet to make significant personnel or coordinator changes to spark a sudden leap in production.

QB stat to know: Since the start of last season, Herbert has been hit 12.6 times per game (only Deshaun Watson has been hit more) and 6.8 times per game in the pocket, which is first among all quarterbacks. Until the Chargers figure out a scheme and an offensive line that get Herbert hit less, the erratic play and terrible interceptions will likely continue.

Second-half storyline: Can Herbert recover anything? The Chargers need to approach 2027 with some scrap of optimism that they haven't totally broken their star franchise quarterback. Herbert needs to shake the uncharacteristic interceptions and avoid major injury for the Chargers to feel like the tailspin is over entering next season. -- Ben Solak

Fantasy nugget: Justin Herbert has thrown zero or one touchdown pass in every game this season. The Chargers use a three-RB rotation, with each having two games with double-digit fantasy points. Ladd McConkey has finished just three games because of injury issues. The Chargers score a league-low 14.1 PPG and are the only offense in the NFL from which you do not need to start anyone. -- Moody

Tennessee Titans
FPI rank: 31

Chances to make the playoffs: Chances to win their division: First-half storyline: The Titans have not found a way to win close games. Tennessee has a 1-6 record in one-score games and has lost six of its seven games by a combined total of 25 points. The Titans consistently put themselves in position to win or tie games late in the fourth quarter, only to come up short because of mistakes.

QB stat to know: All six of Cam Ward's touchdowns this season have come in the fourth quarter, while only one of his five interceptions occurred in that span. Ward has completed 65 of 89 passes for 596 yards in the fourth quarter as well. Ward said he sees the field and reads coverages better and gets into a rhythm as the game progresses.

Second-half storyline: Titans coach Robert Saleh said Ward is his quarterback "this year" when asked about benching him during a rough stretch. Saleh has consistently said Ward will be "a damn good quarterback" despite the struggles. Ward's 304-yard passing performance against the Bengals before the bye week showed he's capable. Ward will have the next nine games to show he should be the quarterback when the Titans open the new stadium in 2027. -- Turron Davenport

Fantasy nugget: Carnell Tate leads the Titans in target (33%) and air yard share (42%). He and Cam Ward were starting to click a bit before Tate was injured. He is an upside candidate to trade for, as the Titans have the second-best remaining schedule for fantasy WRs. -- Moody

Miami Dolphins
FPI rank: 32

Chances to make the playoffs: Chances to win their division: First-half storyline: The Dolphins set out this offseason to rebuild their young core, and it appears they've accomplished that goal. Their first three picks -- Kadyn Proctor, Chris Johnson and Jacob Rodriguez -- all project as long-term starters, while mid-to-late-round picks such as Will Kacmarek, Caleb Douglas and Michael Taaffe have all established themselves as productive players right away.

QB stat to know: Malik Willis averages the third-longest time to throw in the NFL this season and is also pressured at the second-highest rate in the league. At times, it's been an issue. Willis' coaches say that his ability to extend plays is both a "superpower" and something that needs to be balanced -- and that sometimes, it's best to take a checkdown or throw the ball away rather than risk a turnover in search of an explosive play.

Second-half storyline: The Dolphins will continue to let their young players develop, with most of their starting lineup composed of players within their first two NFL seasons. Keep an eye on rookie linebacker Trey Moore, who suffered a lower-body injury in the preseason and has yet to play in the regular season. Miami was excited about his production in training camp and he could add to a defense that has turned in several noteworthy performances in recent weeks. -- Marcel Louis-Jacques

Fantasy nugget: Ollie Gordon II has scored 13.2 fantasy PPG since Week 3 and has the second-best remaining fantasy RB schedule. Malik Willis disappointed in Week 9 but scored 19.8 fantasy PPG in his three prior games. He has the eighth-best remaining fantasy QB schedule and could be a streaming option as QB thins out. -- Moody

stories.headline: Gary Neville slams Man United's 'classless' handling of Michael Carrick sacking
stories.summary: Gary Neville has branded Manchester United "classless" over their actions in the days before Michael Carrick's sacking.
stories.body:
Gary Neville has branded Manchester United "classless" over their actions in the days before Michael Carrick's sacking.

Carrick's departure from the club was finally announced on Thursday morning and Mauricio Pochettino has been lined up to replace him, sources told ESPN.

Official confirmation of Carrick's sacking came after a period of limbo for the former United midfielder, who had reported to Carrington again on Thursday after taking training on Tuesday and Wednesday amid reports he would be removed from his role.

His fate was sealed the day after a meeting took place between the club's powerbrokers in Monaco, where director of football Jason Wilcox and chief executive Omar Berrada travelled to see co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe.

Speaking on the Overlap's Stick to Football podcast, which was recorded prior to Thursday's confirmation, former United defender Neville said the process feels "clumsy."

He said: "We're sat here today recording this programme knowing that Michael Carrick is going to be sacked tomorrow, knowing that they're speaking to Mauricio Pochettino, knowing that they've spoken to [Julian] Nagelsmann, [Eddie] Howe-- and they should be doing that by the way, I'm not saying they shouldn't be doing that.

"But I think the fact they're in Monaco now and they can't sack him today knowing that it's happening, to me it just feels a little bit clumsy, it feels a little bit classless.

"I think if you live in Monaco, you can't leave a guy hanging for 24 or 48 hours just because you live in Monaco, that can't happen."

In May, Carrick was appointed on a permanent basis until 2028 having taken interim charge in January, but the club have struggled so far this term.

United are in the Premier League relegation zone with just eight points having won only one of their 10 league matches this season.

Pochettino has previously managed Tottenham, Paris Saint-Germain and Chelsea before becoming United States head coach and Neville praised the Argentinian for the physical fitness instilled within his teams.

- Michael Carrick sacked by Man United, sources say Mauricio Pochettino close

- Michael Carrick's Man United collapse: The stats behind his sacking

- How Michael Carrick's stint as Man United boss unravelled - a timeline

"One thing we do know about him is he does run his players, he does put physical fitness really at the top of the agenda. He's always had fit teams, whether they've won or not won," Neville said.

"We used to train at Tottenham's training ground when I was with England and they used to have that Tuesday -- I'm calling it terror Tuesday, but it wasn't called terror Tuesday -- it was called something like that, his run was famous at that time in terms of what he does with every team, he does run them.

"They were always fit his teams, to be fair. That's one thing I think he will deal with straight away, he's obviously got a lot of experience now, he knows how to coach a team."

Information from the Press Association contributed to this report.

stories.headline: Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad to continue at Racing Bulls for 2027
stories.summary: Liam Lawson will stay in Formula 1 alongside teammate Arvid Lindblad at Racing Bulls in 2027, ending weeks of speculation about the New Zealander's future.
stories.body:
Liam Lawson will stay in Formula 1 alongside teammate Arvid Lindblad at Racing Bulls in 2027, ending weeks of speculation about the New Zealander's future.

Lawson's place at the team had been under scrutiny in recent weeks, with Red Bull's Bulgarian junior Nikola Tsolov waiting in the wings.

Racing Bulls ended any doubt on Thursday, confirming Lawson and Lindblad will continue together for another year.

Lawson has been one of the year's standout performers, sitting ninth with 89 points, a run of form which continued with a strong showing at last weekend's São Paulo Grand Prix, where he started third and finished seventh. Rookie teammate Lindblad is 11th with 38.

Racing Bulls is fighting for fifth in the constructors' championship.

- Lewis Hamilton visits Gaza border, urges Israel to 'let the aid trucks in'

Team boss Alan Permane, who last week signed a deal to stay in his role until 2029, said Lawson and Lindblad is the strongest lineup the team could ask for.

"We're delighted to be continuing with Liam and Arvid for 2027," Permane said. "Both have demonstrated their ability and potential throughout the season, and we've seen the progress they've made, both individually and as a pairing. I have no doubt that this is the best driver line-up for us, bringing a strong combination of experience and ambition.

"Together, we have a solid foundation to build on the progress made this year, continue pushing ourselves forward and take the next step towards achieving our ambitions in 2027."

stories.headline: NHL Tonight: Bruins-Canadiens, Capitals-Devils highlight Thursday's 11-game slate
stories.summary: Find game previews, betting intel, broadcast information, stats and highlights here.
stories.body:
The NHL's 2026 Global Series hits Finland on Thursday, with a special start time.

But that's just one of 11 games on the schedule, including an Original Six showdown in the Atlantic, two playoff favorites in the Metro vying for critical points and much more.

Read on for a look at what you need to know for each game, including betting info and broadcast details.

Odds are provided by DraftKings and subject to change.

Carolina Hurricanes vs. Seattle Kraken

12 p.m. ET (NHL Network) | CAR -245, O/U: 6.5

Live from Veikkaus Arena in Helsinki, Kaapo Kakko and the Kraken square off against Sebastian Aho and the Hurricanes.

The two teams will meet Thursday and Saturday this week for their lone matchups of the campaign (unless they meet in the Stanley Cup Final). Last season, the teams split the season series, with the home team winning a one-goal game in each instance.

Aho is the Canes' leading scorer with 26 points through 19 games, but the scoring has been spread around; 10 Hurricanes have already hit double digits in points this season.

Kakko trails Berkly Catton on the Kraken's scoring leaderboard (13 to Catton's 14), and six other Seattle players have reached double digits.

Montreal Canadiens at Boston Bruins

7 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | BOS -120, O/U: 6.5

The Bruins and Canadiens have been playing against one another since Dec. 8, 1924. This will be regular season matchup No. 769, and the Habs own a 367-286-103-12 edge in the prior 768.

After this showdown, the teams will not face off again until Jan. 6, with a pair of March contests finishing the season series -- and hopefully there will be a postseason meeting as well.

The Bruins score more (3.72 goals per game to 3.33) and allow fewer (2.28 goals per game to 3.06), but just one point separates them in the standings; the B's are first in the Atlantic with 27 points, while the Habs are second with 26.

Captain David Pastrnak leads the Bruins in scoring (24 points in 18 games); for his career, Pasta has 47 points in 36 career games vs. Montreal.

Minnesota Wild at Toronto Maple Leafs

7 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | MIN -148, O/U: 6.5

Minnesota enters this game having gone 7-1-1 in its last nine, while Toronto is on a four-game losing streak (and lost six of its last seven).

Auston Matthews is having a bounceback campaign, and leads the Leafs in goals (11), assists (17) and obviously points (28). The Wild are paced in goals by Kirill Kaprizov (17) and helpers by Quinn Hughes (21).

The goaltending matchup is the true mismatch, as Jesper Wallstedt leads the league with 12 wins and is among the top five in goals-against average (1.93) and save percentage (.925) while Sergei Bobrovsky has been ... not that. The ex-Panther has a 3-8-2 record, 3.47 GAA and .881 SV%.

Colorado Avalanche at Ottawa Senators

7 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | COL -125, O/U: 6.5

The Avs head to Canada's capital city looking to improve their record against the Atlantic Division to 4-1-0 following wins over Detroit and Toronto in the past six days.

Meanwhile, the Sens are looking to knock off another 2026 playoff team after recent wins over Buffalo and Utah.

And of course... this could be a Stanley Cup Final preview! Stathletes projects this as the 11th highest chances for a Cup Final matchup, at 2.48%.

Will this be the game in which Linus Ullmark returns to the Senators' crease?

Washington Capitals at New Jersey Devils

7 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | NJ -155, O/U: 5.5

As play begins Thursday, the Devils are in the No. 2 slot in the Metro, while the Capitals are the first team out of the bracket, two points behind the Panthers for the second wild card.

Famously (or infamously, depending on your point of view), Connor Hellebuyck did not start the Devils' game Tuesday in Winnipeg; will he back between the pipes for this one?

On the other side, fans are still waiting for Alex Ovechkin to get rolling; through 16 games he has just one goal and four assists. On the plus side, offseason additions Jordan Kyrou (14 points) and Alex Tuch (11 goals) seem to have found their grooves.

Tampa Bay Lightning at Columbus Blue Jackets

7 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | TB -118, O/U: 6.5

The 2026 Hart Trophy winner (Nikita Kucherov) and 2026 Norris Trophy winner (Zach Werenski) have both made waves with various levels of trade request in the past several months, although a one-for-one deal doesn't seem likely.

Beyond that, there isn't a ton of shared history between the clubs -- unless we take a time machine back to 2019 when the Blue Jackets swept the Presidents' Trophy-winning Lightning in the first round of the playoffs. Many players from those rosters are now elsewhere, though Kucherov and Werenski played critical roles.

Despite the trade request, Kucherov continues to lead the Lightning in scoring, and that was boosted after Wednesday's hat trick.

Detroit Red Wings at Florida Panthers

7:30 p.m. ET (ESPN+/Disney+/Hulu) | FLA -170, O/U: 5.5

The Panthers were a popular Cup pick this preseason, but in order to get back to that spot they will need to start winning games against divisional foes. Florida is 0-4-0 against the Atlantic thus far, including a 5-3 loss to these very same Red Wings on Nov. 2.

On the other hand, the Wings were not a popular pick to even make the playoffs, but have come together as a team and fought hard each night out, galvanizing around the reality that Dylan Larkin (and maybe Simon Edvinsson too) won't be on the team anymore.

Five different players scored for Detroit in the previous game, while the Tkachuk Bros managed just one assist apiece. Will that continue on Thursday?

Buffalo Sabres at Chicago Blackhawks

8 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | BUF -142, O/U: 6.5

Louis Crevier revenge game? The 6-foot-8 defenseman was part of the package that Chicago sent to Buffalo in the Bowen Byram blockbuster, though he has been a healthy scratch recently.

Meanwhile, Byram has not played since Oct. 13, and is not expected off of IR in time for this game either. Byram also missed the Oct. 3 game between the teams (a 4-3 win for the Sabres in Buffalo).

The Blackhawks will take a W against anyone these days, entering this contest having lost six in a row and nine of their last 10. Meanwhile, the Sabres are looking to quickly turn the page after being on the wrong side of an 8-3 game Wednesday.

Winnipeg Jets at Dallas Stars

8 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | DAL -205, O/U: 5.5

Are the Jets for real again? After opening the season 4-1-1, Winnipeg went winless in its next nine... before winning four straight, including three Ws against teams currently in playoff position.

Thursday's matchup will thus serve as a litmus test, as one of those non-victories was against Dallas on Oct. 22. The Jets held a 2-1 lead late in that game, before Roope Hintz tied it with 2:00 to go, then won it with a breakaway tally in OT.

Dallas is led in scoring this season by wingers Mikko Rantanen (21 points in 17 games) and Jason Robertson (19 in 17), while Winnipeg is led by winger Kyle Connor (21 in 19) and center Mark Scheifele (19 in 19).

St. Louis Blues at Utah Mammoth

9 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | UTA -135, O/U: 6.5

Following a loss to the Golden Knights on Wednesday, the Mammoth head home to host the Blues.

St. Louis is enjoying the benefits of Joel Hofer's breakout season in goal, but has not been scoring enough to make a real run up the standings. As play begins Thursday, they sit seventh in the Central Division, three points back of the Mammoth for the final wild-card playoff spot.

Utah has the opposite problem, as it is tied for eighth in scoring (3.50 goals per game), but 25th in goals against per game (also 3.50). Will GM Bill Armstrong make another trade to fix the situation?

New York Islanders at Los Angeles Kings

10 p.m. ET (ESPN+/Disney+/Hulu) | LA -135, O/U: 5.5

In Thursday's nightcap, the Isles continue their tour of California after losing 3-2 in a shootout to the Sharks on Monday -- and prior to a showdown against the Ducks on Saturday.

The Kings are still trying to figure things out under new head coach Peter Laviolette (and in the first season without Anze Kopitar), losing their last two games by a combined score of 8-2.

This is the second game between the teams this season (thus concluding the season series). L.A. won the first thanks to two first-period goals by Artemi Panarin and the OT game-winner by Brandt Clarke.

What do Matthew Schaefer & Co. have in store for their hosts on Thursday evening?

stories.headline: Brewers' Misiorowski, Yanks' Schlittler crowned unanimous Cy Young winners
stories.summary: Milwaukee's Jacob Misiorowski and New York's Cam Schlittler capped dominant 2026 seasons by sweeping all 30 first-place votes to win their respective Cy Young Awards.
stories.body:
Jacob Misiorowski and Cam Schlittler, the two most dominant starters in baseball in 2026, were named unanimous Cy Young Award winners Wednesday.

Misiorowski, the ace of the World Series champion Milwaukee Brewers, received all 30 first-place votes for the National League honor in his first full big league season, finishing ahead of Cristopher Sanchez of the Philadelphia Phillies in second and Chris Sale of the Atlanta Braves in third.

Schlittler, the New York Yankees' breakout No. 1 starter, swept the American League award also in his first full major league campaign, with Dylan Cease of the Toronto Blue Jays in second place and Parker Messick of the Cleveland Guardians in third.

San Diego Padres closer Mason Miller and Toronto Blue Jays closer Louis Varland won the Baseball Writers' Association of America's inaugural Reliever of the Year award in their respective leagues.

Varland earned 16 of the 30 first-place votes for the AL honor. The right-hander's 1.27 ERA across 78 innings was the lowest in the majors among qualified relievers. He finished the season with 35 saves in 71 appearances.

Miller took the NL award unanimously after logging one of the best reliever seasons in recent history. The right-hander was an overwhelming force late in games, logging a 1.67 ERA with 38 saves and 129 strikeouts -- the most in baseball among relievers -- in 70 innings across 66 appearances. He finished with a 47.6% strikeout rate, sixth all time among pitchers with at least 50 innings pitched.

Miller's 101.4 mph average fastball velocity was tops in the majors. Misiorowski, incredibly, wasn't far off.

Misiorowski, 24, went 16-5 with a 1.80 ERA, 0.80 WHIP and 252 strikeouts in 30 starts across 174⅔ innings -- leading the majors in ERA, WHIP, and strikeouts -- as the Brewers won an MLB-best 103 games. His 6.6 fWAR led all pitchers. His 232 ERA+ was the best for a full season since Pedro Martinez recorded a 291 ERA+ in 2000.

He became the fourth Cy Young Award winner in Brewers franchise history, joining Corbin Burnes (2021), Pete Vuckovich (1982), and Rollie Fingers (1981). He is the first pitcher since Randy Johnson in 2001 to win the Cy Young and World Series in the same season. He is the third pitcher since 2000 to win both the Cy Young Award and World Series in the same season.

"I'm going to go hunting next week with my dad," Misiorowski said. "And that quiet time in the stand is really going to be my opportunity to think about this year. And think about all the positives that we had, and what to work on and what I need to do, to do this again next year."

The historic performance was fueled by unprecedented velocity. Misiorowski's fastball averaged 100.6 mph, unparalleled territory for a full-time starting pitcher. He threw more than 1,000 pitches at 100 mph or faster -- more than double the record Jordan Hicks set in 2018. He threw more pitches at 101 mph or faster than every other pitcher combined from 2008 through 2026. His fastest pitch, a 105.5 mph heater in June against Pete Crow-Armstrong, was the fastest pitch ever thrown by a starting pitcher in the Statcast era.

The 6-foot-7 Misiorowski took the league by storm as a rookie in 2025, controversially making the NL All-Star team as a replacement after only five starts. But he struggled down the stretch with a 5.36 ERA over his final 10 outings before compiling a 1.50 ERA in 12 innings across three relief appearances in the postseason. This year, he harnessed the heat.

This year, he harnessed the heat. Misiorowski carried a 3.31 ERA over his first six starts through April before establishing himself as the best pitcher in the sport with a 1.46 ERA in 142 innings over his final 24 starts. The stretch included a one-hit shutout with 15 strikeouts and no walks against the Phillies on June 12. He finished the season with 10 double-digit strikeout outings before posting a 1.89 ERA in 19 innings across four playoff starts, including the Brewers' World Series-clinching Game 5 win less than a year-and-a-half after making his major league debut.

"It's happened really quick," Misiorowski said. "It's crazy, the opportunity that I got in front of me and being able to take a hold of that and run with it is really cool. It's been a crazy two years, year and a half or whatever it is. It's been fun."

Schlittler, 25, became the seventh Yankee -- and the first since Gerrit Cole in 2023 -- to win the award. Of the seven, only he, Ron Guidry, and Whitey Ford were homegrown.

He didn't throw quite as hard as his NL counterpart, but his three-fastball mix confounded hitters all season. He complemented a four-seam fastball that routinely touched triple digits and averaged 98 mph with a 94.6 mph cutter, 97.8 mph sinker, and power curveball he incorporated more later in the season.

The Massachusetts native -- and Boston Red Sox fan growing up -- finished 14-6 with a 1.95 ERA and 239 strikeouts in 193⅔ innings over 33 starts for a pitching staff that posted the best ERA in the majors. He gave up one run or fewer in 21 starts. He was at his best away from Yankee Stadium, logging a 1.16 ERA in 17 road starts. He led the AL in ERA, fWAR (6.2), and ERA+ (215). Only Spud Chandler (1.64 in 1943) and Guidry (1.74 in 1978) have posted a lower ERA as qualified starters in franchise history.

He plowed through lineups with an uncommon confidence and fire, becoming invaluable for a Yankees rotation that dealt with extended absences from Cole, Max Fried, and Carlos Rodon.

"Realistically, I look at it and I'm just happy," Schlittler said. "The goal, honestly, coming into the season was to stay healthy, be consistent, and make all my starts. That's something I was able to do."

A seventh-round pick out of Northeastern in 2022, Schlittler flew under the radar as he rose through the minor leagues because his stuff did not scream dominance. His fastball velocity averaged in the low 90s in his first full professional season in 2023. But with a few delivery tweaks and added muscle, the velocity gradually climbed until he reached 100 mph for the first time in his major league debut at Yankee Stadium in July 2025.

He found his footing in his fourth start three weeks later and was a revelation down the stretch and into the postseason. In Game 3 of the AL Wild Card Series, he held the Red Sox scoreless over eight innings with 12 strikeouts and no walks, which solidified his standing among the game's best pitchers.

The Yankees entered 2026 with Schlittler firmly in their rotation. They hoped for continued growth from a resounding rookie campaign. He exceeded all expectations with one of the greatest pitching seasons in the franchise's history. He's already shooting for more.

"I definitely could have had a better season," Schlittler said. "Obviously, I had a few hiccups along the road. Realistically, I think there's things I can get better at and that's not going to be specifically in one area of the game. But just being out there on the mound and making certain adjustments in the game. Again, I feel like this season was great, but as you look at how I finished, things could have definitely been better."

Also Wednesday, Miller was a unanimous winner of the Trevor Hoffman NL Reliever of the Year Award, and the Rays' Bryan Baker was named the Mariano Rivera AL Reliever of the Year. The Hoffman and Rivera honors are voted on by a panel of former relievers and are separate from the BBWAA awards, which are voted on by BBWAA members.

Other MLB awards handed out Wednesday:

Comeback Player of the Year: Yordan Alvarez, Houston Astros (AL); Zack Wheeler, Philadelphia Phillies (NL)
Edgar Martinez award (outstanding DH): Yordan Alvarez
Hank Aaron award (top offense performer): Yordan Alvarez (AL); Pete Crow-Armstrong, Chicago Cubs (NL)
Executive of the Year: Erik Neander, Rays

stories.headline: MMA stars Merab Dvalishvili, Usman Nurmagomedov brawl at hotel in Abu Dhabi
stories.summary: MMA stars Merab Dvalishvili and Usman Nurmagomedov got into a public brawl at a hotel in Abu Dhabi on Wednesday.
stories.body:
Former UFC bantamweight champion Merab Dvalishvili and PFL lightweight champion Usman Nurmagomedov were involved in a physical altercation Wednesday in Abu Dhabi, with video of the incident widely circulated on social media.

Dvalishvili, who is in Abu Dhabi ahead of Saturday's Real American Freestyle event, posted a video of his bloodied face after the scuffle. Multiple videos of the incident showed Nurmagomedov, whose older brother, Umar, lost a bantamweight title fight to Dvalishvili in 2025, approach Dvalishvili from behind and slap him in the face.

Former UFC lightweight champion Ilia Topuria, who is friends with Dvalishvili, shared video of the encounter online. Following the initial slap, Dvalishvili attempts to go after Nurmagomedov. A chaotic scene quickly unfolded, involving multiple members from the camps of both fighters. In his video afterward, Dvalishvili refers to Nurmagomedov and his camp as "snakes."

"What a sneaky way, guys," Dvalishvili says. "What kind of fighters you guys are? What kind of man does this? If you want to try, let's do it the real way."

Wednesday's confrontation marks the latest in a long-running feud between Dvalishvili and the Nurmagomedov team. Before his win over Umar in January 2025, Dvalishvili referred to Umar as "spoiled" and accused the Dagestani of being disrespectful. The two camps were involved in a brief altercation in July at another RAF event in Georgia.

Both Merab and Umar are scheduled to compete at RAF on Saturday. Dvalishvili faces former UFC title challenger Marlon Moraes, while Nurmagomedov will wrestle former UFC champion Urijah Faber.

Usman Nurmagomedov is currently in a state of restricted free agency, with much speculation whether he will leave the PFL to fight in the UFC in 2027.

stories.headline: Despite injury and illness, Gus Teixeira is still one of this year's top prospects
stories.summary: Gus Teixeira spent much of his top-age year battling injury and illness, but still found a way to be in contention to be the top pick in the open pool, writes Japser Chellappah.
stories.body:
Gustavo Teixeira had a brilliant top-age campaign. He's worked his way into pick 1 conversations, and is locked into the first handful of selections on draft night.

His success is made all the more impressive considering what's played out behind the scenes.

"I had the ankle injury at the start of the year in the first praccy game," Teixeira tells ESPN.

"It was kind of a bit annoying because every week I thought I'd be playing but it just got pushed back. I had the calf injury, I was out for five or six weeks. I rehabbed that, played a game and then the foot pulled up sore and that's why I'm not testing [at the AFL Draft combine].

"I've also been sick for basically the whole year with a virus."

Teixeira, a powerful forward-half midfielder, played valiantly through glandular fever-like symptoms that didn't get diagnosed until the conclusion of the National Championships.

He was playing games deep in the forward 50 but still finding himself short of breath and unable to hit top gear. After being diagnosed with a severe iron deficiency and receiving an infusion he felt the energy he'd been lacking return, but not before a calf injury linked to his virus took Teixeira out for all but one game in the back half of the season.

Most top-10 chances at the AFL Draft thrive off injury-free seasons where they can continually put their name up in lights. Teixeira couldn't do that this year, so he made his moments count.

His first game back from an ankle concern was in a Vic Metro trial game where he showed his worth, kicking two goals from 20 disposals in a best afield display.

"It was a good day out, I was pretty happy with that. It was annoying I couldn't do a bit more of that throughout the year but I'm sure I can do that in the future."

Teixeira had locked himself into Metro's National Championships outfit by halftime, showing off the power and class that recruiters covet.

At the National Championships he was playing under duress from his undiagnosed virus, but he still took the opportunity to show his value deep in attack.

"Obviously I was sick so I was resting a bit, I was sore the first week and they wanted me to play more forward. I kicked a few goals and they wanted me to stay down forward and that's where I was able to impact the most," he tells ESPN.

Teixeira claimed All-Australian honours, booting seven goals in his four outings including a best on ground demolition of the Allies where he kicked four goals from 22 touches.

It was an element of his game that proved his worth outside of the centre square. Teixeira got to dangerous spots and created separation with proactive running, and from there was able to demonstrate his cleanliness and class to make his chances count.

"I've always thought I want to be a midfielder, I want to play in there. Skills are very important as a midfielder so you've got to be clean and you've got to be able to kick. I'm just chipping away at it and improving."

Teixeira is of Brazilian descent via his father Matt, who was born in the city of Belo Horizonte before moving to Australia when he was 25.

He brings Gus back to Brazil every year, and that connection to a non-English speaking country would allow Teixeira to join zoned club St Kilda's Next Generation Academy if not for friction points within the AFL's own NGA rules.

"Belo Horizonte is just inland of Rio... It's like the size of Melbourne but no one's really heard of it. It's a fully different culture and it's always great to go back," he explains.

"The AFL changed the rules for the regions this year, so they allow South American people this year but you need to be in it for three years. I would've only been in it for a year... my younger siblings are in it now. I've got a brother, Eddie, who's 12 and my sister Lucy who's 14."

Like a host of the top prospects this year, Teixeira has been an Essendon supporter his whole life. The Bombers have the top pick and Teixeira is within that bracket of the pool.

"I haven't thought about the Bombers pick-wise, but just the club and thinking about what it would be like obviously going to the Bombers, it'd be great at the moment. They're getting in some good coaches and they've got some good players coming through.

"Really though I'd be stoked to get drafted to any club, moving interstate would be a pretty cool experience. I'm always trying to get the best out of myself, I've always tried to be the best at everything and just put my best foot forward so I'll do that anywhere."

stories.headline: Will MLS teams' regular-season momentum last the two weeks before the playoffs start?
stories.summary: The MLS regular season ended on Saturday, but it will be nearly two weeks before the playoffs begin. It's a long time for a hot team to cool off.
stories.body:
With MLS Cup playoffs approaching, one word that continually comes up is "momentum." Does a team have it? If so, how can it maintain it, especially against the league's better teams? If not, how can the team get it back?

That said, the postseason does plenty to wreck the very concept of momentum. The league's playoffs are as unpredictable as it gets. Brackets are routinely demolished.

Nobody knows better the fickle nature of momentum than former MLS player and current Apple TV broadcaster Dax McCarty. He was part of the 2013 Supporters' Shield-winning Red Bull New York side that was eliminated in the Eastern Conference semifinal by the Houston Dynamo, thanks in part to a red card in the first leg to standout defender Jamison Olave.

McCarty was also part of the 2024 Atlanta United side that squeaked into the playoffs on Decision Day, beat CF Montréal in the wild card and then sprung an incredible upset against the juggernaut that was that year's Inter Miami side in Round 1. The win over Miami was aided by Atlanta keeper Brad Guzan performing physics-defying feats of gymnastics in the Five Stripes' goal.

"If the playoffs have taught us anything over the course of Major League Soccer's existence, it's that [you should] throw all that stuff out the window at times," McCarty told ESPN. "Throw tactics out the window, throw out momentum, throw out form, because one crazy play, one red card, one fluky goal can be the difference between advancing or your season being over."

Yet momentum is something that is still prized by coaches. In a world of fine margins, if you believe that you're going to win because of how you're playing in the moment, then the chances are better that the form will continue.

"I think momentum always matters, whether it's going into the postseason or whether it's the second game of the season," Houston Dynamo manager Ben Olsen said. "I think it matters mostly just because you want your team peaking around playoff time, and being the best version of themselves."

San Jose Earthquakes boss Bruce Arena stressed that momentum is as much a state of mind as it is about results. That's especially true if a coach feels his team is still short of its best.

"It doesn't have to be a terrific run going into the playoffs, but you have to have a team going in with confidence," he said. "You need to have a pretty good idea about what your team's about and how you want to go about your business in the playoffs.

"Probably the psychological part of it is more important than actually the tactical part of it. You just got to get inside the team and make sure that they enter the game with the confidence that they can get a result."

That appears to be true for the Quakes, who finished the season by going 4W-7D-2L. Houston, who faces San Jose in the first round, went a more sobering 2W-7D-4L.

At this stage of the season, teams have already been together for 10 months, so a manager is bound to know what makes his team tick. That doesn't mean said manager's work is done. There could be collaborative meetings in terms of refining how the team wants to approach a certain opponent.

Individual meetings might be needed as well to bolster the confidence of a particular player. A lineup change or a subtle tactical tweak could help a team as well. Arena stressed there is no formula for how he handles things.

"I think I've been in seven MLS Cup finals and won five of them, and I don't think I can tell you that I had the same approach to any of them," Arena said. "Every one was different."

The issue of momentum -- whether trying to maintain it or generate it -- faces some tricky obstacles this postseason. Following last Saturday's Decision Day, the teams that qualified for the playoffs will get around two weeks between matches due to the FIFA international window.

With rhythm broken, the playing field would appear to be more level. That provokes myriad questions in terms of approach. McCarty said the break "absolutely" has an effect on rhythm, momentum and potential injuries.

"How hard do you push your players? You want your players in form, but you also don't want them to get injured," McCarty said. "How hard are the coaches going to push their players?"

There seem to be two paths a manager can take. They either have a scrimmage against another MLS team, or they have an intra-squad match, albeit one in a stadium with referees, the better to simulate a real match. There are pros and cons to both. With injury prevention paramount, playing against another MLS team would appear to offer less control on the level of physicality.

"I think you would want to keep it in-house in terms of an intra-squad scrimmage to try to keep your players fit, to try to keep your players sharp, and with the very real caveat before the game to say, 'Listen, there are no dumb tackles. There are no slide tackles,'" McCarty said. "If you are an Inter Miami fan or a New England Revolution fan or a Nashville SC fan, you're telling young players that might be involved, 'You are not allowed to touch Hany Mukhtar. You're not allowed to touch Carles Gil. You're not allowed to touch [Lionel] Messi.'

"Those are the very clear expectations you have to set. But guess what? That doesn't actually give you a realistic playoff feel. It's whoever can find the right balance, whoever can be at their sharpest and fittest going into these first rounds of games, is going to like their chances."

Olsen indicated he wasn't particularly worried about dealing with the break, although he declined to specify which kind of scrimmage he would utilize. His thinking is that he's dealt with bye weeks so many times over the years that, "We all have a recipe for that."

Sure, he might change a few things here and there, but the concepts remain consistent, and he trusts his sports science department to get things right.

"There's a physical periodization, and there will be a tactical periodization from our side, but it's one that again has been, we've delivered, I don't know, 10, 15 times in the last three and a half years," he said.

Olsen admitted, though, that this time there's a twist.

"You're coming out of this into the most important game of the year, and that's a little bit new," he said.

Arena said he'll be going the intra-squad scrimmage route, although the international window brings another wrinkle to his preparations. What kind of condition will his four players that go away for international duty be in when they get back is a giant unknown.

"If you have players getting called up for international duty, they're likely starters in your team as well," Arena said. "So there's a lot of challenging things for coaches and players as you enter the playoffs. And this year it's been even more complicated because of the international window and the poor planning on the part of Major League Soccer."

This much is clear. Every manager will be trying to build momentum, wherever they can find it.

stories.headline: Dirk Kuyt leaves Fenerbahce a week after defeating Liverpool
stories.summary: Dirk Kuyt left Fenerbahce on Wednesday, one week after guiding the team as interim coach to beat his old club Liverpool in the Champions League.
stories.body:
ISTANBUL -- Dirk Kuyt left Fenerbahce on Wednesday, one week after guiding the team as interim coach to beat his old club Liverpool in the Champions League.

The former Netherlands forward took charge of that 3-2 win in Istanbul despite the club already having made a deal with Emre Belözoğlu to take over.

Kuyt returned in July to Fenerbahce, where he played from 2012-15, to assist coach Ismail Kartal who resigned last month.

"We thank you from the bottom of our hearts for all that you have contributed to these colors," Fenerbahce said in a social media post announcing Kuyt's exit. "Today we say goodbye to you but your place in this big family will never change."

Belözoğlu, a former captain of the club, takes over a team sixth in the Turkish league and 19th in the 36-team Champions League standings.

Fenerbahce's next Champions League opponent is Shakhtar Donetsk in London on Nov. 25.
